Destination: Big Island, Hawaii (Kona 4 nights + Volcano 3 nights)
Why it's good for you two: Most varied week in the set: an actively erupting volcano (Kilauea has had 56 lava-fountain episodes since Dec 2024), beaches, manta-ray night snorkel, Mauna Kea stargazing, and reliably warm weather on the Kona side. Hawaii was a must-include and this is the island that best fits hikers.
Top hikes: Kilauea Iki (4 mi loop across a crater floor); Pololu Valley lookout trail; Captain Cook Monument / Ka'awaloa trail (snorkel at the end); Mauna Kea summit area / Onizuka visitor station; Akaka Falls
Museums & food highlights: Pu'uhonua o Honaunau National Historical Park, Volcano Art Center, Kona coffee farm tours, Hilo Farmers Market; poke, loco moco, shave ice, Kona coffee
January weather (normals; source in Sour: Kona: high ~81F / low ~69F (NOAA 1991-2020); rain on ~1 in 4 days near Kona (ERA5 2015-25). Volcano village (3,700 ft) is much cooler and wetter, so bring layers.
Main downsides / advisories: Most expensive option. Eruption timing is unpredictable (fountaining episodes are usually under 12 hours and separated by pauses of 2+ weeks), so seeing live lava is a bonus, not a promise. Some park areas are closed for eruption hazards and summit construction. Lighter on museums.

Why it's good for you two: Mexico's food and craft capital in its dry season: hot sunny days with cool nights, Zapotec ruins, mezcal country, weaving villages, and real mountain hiking in the Sierra Norte. Best value per day of any option.
Top hikes: Sierra Norte / Pueblos Mancomunados village-to-village hikes (guided); Hierve el Agua petrified waterfalls; Monte Alban hilltop ruins; Mitla; El Tule tree
Museums & food highlights: Museo de las Culturas (Santo Domingo), Textile Museum, Ethnobotanical Garden, Teotitlan del Valle weavers; mole, tlayudas, mezcal tastings, Mercado 20 de Noviembre, cooking classes
January weather (normals; source in Sour: High ~84F / low ~51F (Mexico's SMN 1991-2020); rain on ~1% of early-January days (ERA5 2015-25)
Flight or drive time from LAX / Hawthorn: No nonstop. ~7.5h with a stop in Mexico City (Aeromexico); cheapest Jan 5-12 fare is ~10.5h with a stop on United
Main downsides / advisories: Connecting flight both ways. Cold mornings (~50F). US State Dept Level 2 (increased caution) for Oaxaca state; US government staff may not travel to the Isthmus region, which is far from Oaxaca City.

Destination: La Paz + Todos Santos, Baja California Sur
Why it's good for you two: Shortest flight of any abroad option to warm, dry desert-by-the-sea. Boat day to Isla Espiritu Santo (sea lions, snorkeling), whale sharks in La Paz bay in season, then the surf-and-art town of Todos Santos. Best for outdoors plus easy logistics.
Top hikes: Balandra Bay and El Mirador trail; Sierra de la Laguna foothill hikes (Canon de la Zorra waterfall); Punta Lobos and Las Palmas beach walk near Todos Santos; kayaking Espiritu Santo
Museums & food highlights: Malecon de La Paz, La Paz Regional Museum of Anthropology, Todos Santos galleries; fish and shrimp tacos, chocolate clams, Baja farm-to-table restaurants near Todos Santos
January weather (normals; source in Sour: La Paz: high ~78F / low ~54F (SMN 1991-2020); Todos Santos ~77F / ~59F (ERA5); rain on ~2-3% of days
Best dates: Jan 5-12 (nonstop $914 vs $1,068 for two, or $1,328 for the Jan 2-9 nonstop)
Main downsides / advisories: You need a rental car, and Mexican liability insurance makes it pricier than the base rate. Ocean is cool (wetsuit helps). Thinner museum scene. State Dept Level 2 for Baja California Sur.

Why it's good for you two: World-class museums and food at a bargain, cheapest flights in the set. Day trips to Teotihuacan and volcano hikes. Less 'warm-weather' than the others: sunny days but cold nights.
Top hikes: Nevado de Toluca crater lakes (day trip, about 14,000 ft); Desierto de los Leones; Teotihuacan pyramids; Chapultepec
Museums & food highlights: National Museum of Anthropology, Frida Kahlo Museum, Palacio de Bellas Artes, Museo Soumaya; tacos al pastor, mercados, Roma/Condesa restaurants
January weather (normals; source in Sour: High ~72F / low ~47F (SMN 1991-2020, Tacubaya); rain on ~7% of days
Best dates: Jan 5-12 (cheapest $742 with stops or $974 nonstop for two, vs $996 Jan 2-9)
Main downsides / advisories: At 7,350 ft, nights are cold, and altitude plus air quality can bother some people. A big city, not a beach. State Dept Level 2.

Destination: Maui, Hawaii (Kihei base): the Hawaii alternative
Why it's good for you two: If you'd rather have Maui: Haleakala sunrise, the Road to Hana, peak whale season in January, and great beaches. Polished and easy, but lodging costs more than on the Big Island and there's no lava.
Top hikes: Pipiwai Trail (bamboo forest, Waimoku Falls); Haleakala Sliding Sands trail; Waihe'e Ridge; Hoapili trail
Museums & food highlights: Maui Ocean Center, Bailey House Museum, Hawaiian Islands Humpback Whale Sanctuary; poke, Paia and Upcountry food, farm stands
January weather (normals; source in Sour: Kahului: high ~82F / low ~64F (NOAA 1991-2020); rain on ~1 in 5 days (ERA5)
Main downsides / advisories: Most expensive lodging of all the options. Haleakala sunrise needs a $1 reservation (plus the $30 park fee) that sells out. Road to Hana is a long driving day.

Why it's good for you two: Easy and cheap: no flights, desert hiking plus Palm Springs pools, mid-century design and food. Good fallback if you'd rather keep cash for a bigger trip.
Top hikes: Ryan Mountain; Lost Palms Oasis; Hidden Valley; Skull Rock; Tahquitz Canyon; Palm Springs Aerial Tramway to the San Jacinto trails (can be snowy)
Museums & food highlights: Palm Springs Art Museum, Sunnylands, Moorten Botanical Garden; date shakes, Palm Springs restaurant scene
January weather (normals; source in Sour: Palm Springs: high ~71F / low ~48F; Twentynine Palms (Joshua Tree): high ~63F / low ~42F (NOAA 1991-2020)
Flight or drive time from LAX / Hawthorn: About 2.5-3h drive each way (estimate, about 140 mi to Joshua Tree)
Best dates: Either window (no flights). Weekdays are quieter.
Main downsides / advisories: Only mildly warm: Joshua Tree nights get close to freezing. Small chance of storms. Feels less like a getaway.

Top hikes: Boca de Tomatlan to Las Animas / Quimixto coastal trail; Vallarta Botanical Garden; Cerro de la Cruz lookout
Museums & food highlights: Vallarta Botanical Garden, Malecon sculptures; street tacos, seafood, Zona Romantica restaurants
January weather (normals; source in Sour: High ~80F / low ~62F (WMO normals); rain on ~6% of days
Main downsides / advisories: QA DOWNGRADE: Jalisco is US State Dept Level 3 'Reconsider travel' (May 29, 2026). The government-staff travel bans cover southern Jalisco, not PV itself, but it is still the highest-risk rating in this set. Fewer museums and more resort feel.

Why it's good for you two: Cheapest overall. Saguaro hiking, a world-class desert museum, Sonoran food (Tucson is a UNESCO City of Gastronomy). But it's cool, not warm, in January.
Top hikes: Sabino Canyon / Seven Falls; Saguaro National Park (Wasson Peak, Hugh Norris); Mount Lemmon (may be snowy); Tumamoc Hill
Museums & food highlights: Arizona-Sonora Desert Museum, Pima Air & Space Museum, Mission San Xavier del Bac; Sonoran hot dogs, carne asada, Mexican food on 4th Ave and South Tucson
Flight or drive time from LAX / Hawthorn: About 7-8h drive each way (estimate, about 490 mi)
Main downsides / advisories: Coolest option, with nights near 40F. Two long drive days use up much of the week. Least 'vacation-warm'.

Destination: Guanacaste, Costa Rica (Tamarindo area): honorable mention
Why it's good for you two: Hottest and greenest option: national parks, wildlife, surf. Dry season starts in January.
Top hikes: Rincon de la Vieja volcano trails and hot springs; Las Catalinas trails; Playa Conchal beach walks
Museums & food highlights: Limited museums; casados, ceviche, sodas (local diners)
Flight or drive time from LAX / Hawthorn: 5h40 nonstop on Jan 2-9 only; the cheapest Jan 5-12 fare has 3 stops (~10.5h)
Best dates: Jan 5-12 if you accept connections; Jan 2-9 for the nonstop ($1,872 for two)
Main downsides / advisories: Flights are pricey or involve long connections. Driving is slow and mandatory rental insurance is expensive. It's a 2-week trip squeezed into 7 nights. State Dept Level 2.
